topic: Decision Making to Improve Operational Performance
subject: business-studies

moments.title: East India Company chartered
moments.body: On 31 December 1600, the Honourable East India Company receives its royal charter. It is a joint-stock company: shares are sold to investors, who share profits in proportion to their stake. It was not the first joint-stock venture, but it became the largest and longest-lived.
moments.takeaway: Pooling capital from many small investors makes ventures possible that no individual could finance.

moments.title: Limited liability becomes general
moments.body: The Limited Liability Act 1855 and the Joint Stock Companies Act 1856, consolidated in 1862, generalise limited liability incorporation for the first time. Shareholders' losses are capped at their investment; personal assets are protected.
moments.takeaway: The combination of joint-stock ownership and limited liability is the legal foundation of the modern public company.

now.title: Companies today
now.body: By 2024 the UK had over 5 million registered companies (Companies House). The corporate form has been extended (B Corps, public benefit corporations, employee ownership trusts) but the joint-stock limited company remains the dominant structure for serious commercial activity.
now.open_questions: Should limited liability extend to all corporate harm? Recent debates on environmental and human rights liability test the limits.

reflection: Limited liability was controversial in 1855 — critics argued it would encourage reckless speculation. The corporate form we treat as natural is a 19th-century legal innovation.
